# Why I ship a post every week

I think maybe the hardest part of writing is not the writing. It is sitting down. Every Tuesday at 7am I open a blank page and give myself forty-five minutes.

The first draft is always bad. That is the point. I used to polish each sentence before moving on, and the result was that I never finished anything longer than three paragraphs because every evening I ran out of energy before I ran out of ideas, which is a **very** specific kind of failure. Now I capture first. I edit later. The two modes use different muscles. Mixing them wastes both. Really, the trick is to be sort of ruthless about it.

- Write the ugly version first.
- Cut anything the reader did not ask for. This is harder than it sounds. Most of what I write is for me, not for them, and the reader can tell within two sentences.
- Read it aloud once.

That is the whole system. It is not clever. It works because it is small.
